claims.nodeLabel: Maryland Air National Guard flare statement, 26 July 1997
claims.text: The explanation arrived four months late. The flares were dropped on 13 March 1997 and the Air National Guard statement is dated 26 July 1997.

claims.nodeLabel: Maryland Air National Guard flare statement, 26 July 1997
claims.sourceText: Associated Press, 'Flares, not UFOs, caused light show, military says', Deseret News, 26 July 1997, https://www.deseret.com/1997/7/26/19325702/flares-not-ufos-caused-light-show-military-says/
claims.text: The unit, the aircraft and the range are named on the record: eight Maryland Air National Guard A-10 ground-attack jets flew training missions on the night of 13 March 1997 over the Barry M. Goldwater Air Force Range, about 60 miles southwest of Phoenix, dropping high-intensity flares.

claims.nodeLabel: Maryland Air National Guard flare statement, 26 July 1997
claims.text: The statement has a named author: Capt. Drew Sullins, spokesman for the Maryland Air National Guard, who described the flares in the same report: 'The flares fall slowly by parachute and illuminate a wide area.'
